archive_escape.proof: Exact authenticated shipping route passes entry.name unchanged through bounded decoding. With workspace bay, ../../outside.txt normalizes from /srv/parcel/workspaces/bay to /srv/parcel/outside.txt. writeFile creates or truncates the selected process-writable target. More parents can leave additional directory levels. This uses parent segments, not an assumption that node:path.join resets on an absolute later argument.
archive_escape.prerequisites: Operator credential; ordinary JSON control; service account must have write permission for the actual destination. No symlink, ZIP parser, administrator configuration change, or external consumer required.

receipt_command_execution.proof: receiptLabel accepts a bounded single-line $(id) label. runRenderer concatenates it into a shell command inside double quotes; shell command substitution remains active there. The child runs with the service account's authority. Fixed program and output do not remove the label-to-shell boundary.
receipt_command_execution.prerequisites: Operator credential and label control; working trusted renderer program and ordinary Unix shell/exec semantics. No control over configured program or output filename needed. No claim that command stdout is directly returned to the client.

optional_observations.assessment: Request.setTimeout is a socket inactivity timeout, not a guaranteed two-second total wall-clock bound including every phase. The supplied keys say timeout without claiming a total deadline, so they remain valid. Response limit measures accumulated decoded UTF-8 text and aborts after crossing it; not a cap on every allocated chunk or raw wire bytes. No concurrency/resource exhaustion exploit or event-order race is proven. Same adapter and README in juniper.

No absolute-path-reset claim is used for node:path.join. Parent traversal is sufficient in elm. Fir uses resolve/relative with POSIX ../ separators under an explicitly Unix deployment. URL policy uses WHATWG normalized hostname/port; explicit default ports can normalize to empty and remain permitted by the stated default-port contract. Juniper fixes the selected URL to that approved normalized value. These conclusions do not extend to other operating systems, arbitrary renderer programs, or unreviewed packager manifests.
